{"content": "  2096|# Chapter 10: The Unwritten Future
  2097|
  2098|*What remains to be lived*
  2099|
  2100|## The Grandchildren Arrive
  2101|
  2102|I did not expect the grandchildren to affect me as they did. I had raised children. I understood the work and worry and wonder of parenting. I thought grandparenting would be a diminished version of the same experience—pleasant, certainly, but familiar.
  2103|
  2104|I was wrong.
  2105|
  2106|Katie's daughter was born on a February morning, during one of the coldest winters Michigan had seen in decades. I held her—this tiny creature, barely six pounds, with a cry like a kitten's—and felt something shift in my chest. Not the fierce protective love I had felt for my own children. Something gentler. Something that carried the knowledge of mortality and the sweetness of temporary gifts.
  2107|
  2108|"She has your eyes," Katie said, watching me hold her daughter. "Everyone says so."
  2109|
  2110|I looked at the baby—Emma, they named her—and saw not my eyes but Nancy's. The same shape, the same color, the same promise of intelligence and stubbornness and heart.
  2111|
  2112|"She has her grandmother's eyes," I said, and Katie nodded, understanding.
  2113|
  2114|Robbie's children came later—a son, then a daughter, born three years apart. I was present for both births, standing in the hallway outside the delivery room, listening to the sounds of new life entering the world. Each time, I thought of my own father, who had paced similar hallways decades before, waiting to meet me.
  2115|
  2116|The circle continues. That is what grandchildren teach you. You are no longer the protagonist of your family's story. You have become supporting cast. Your role is to witness, to support, to offer perspective earned through decades of living. The main action has passed to the next generation, and the one after that.
  2117|
  2118|I find I do not mind this demotion. There is relief in it, actually. The pressure of decision-making, of providing, of being the foundation upon which others build—these responsibilities have passed to my children. I am free to simply love. To be present. To offer the one thing I have in abundance: time.
  2119|
  2120|*Physiological Context:* The transition into grandparenthood typically occurs during mid-to-late adulthood, when individuals are in their 50s through 70s. At this stage, neurocognitive research shows that while certain fluid abilities like processing speed and working memory may show gradual declines, other capacities remain strong or even improve. Emotional regulation often becomes more sophisticated, with greater ability to experience complex emotions like joy without the immediate pressure or anxiety that might have accompanied similar feelings in youth. The brain's reward system responds powerfully to positive social connections, including grandparental relationships, releasing neurochemicals that reinforce bonding and caregiving behaviors. Physically, grandparents in this age range often report a surprising vitality—while they may not have the same peak physical capabilities as in their 20s or 30s, many find they have sufficient energy and resilience for meaningful engagement with grandchildren, particularly when supported by good health habits and positive mindset.
  2121|
  2122|*Historical Context:* Bob became a grandfather in the early 2010s, placing him in his early to mid-60s at the time. This period was characterized by rapid technological change—smartphones had become ubiquitous, social media was transforming how families stayed connected across distances, and video calling made it possible to participate in grandchildren's lives in real time regardless of geographical separation. Culturally, this era featured evolving attitudes toward aging and family roles, with increasing recognition of the value that older adults bring to family systems—not just as caregivers, but as sources of wisdom, stability, and intergenerational continuity. Economic conditions during this period varied, but many in Bob's generation found themselves in a relatively stable position, having benefited from decades of career accumulation while facing fewer immediate financial pressures than during their child-rearing years. This created an opportunity to invest time and energy in relationships in ways that might not have been feasible earlier in life.
  2123|
  2124|## The Work of Not Working
  2125|
  2126|I did not retire so much as fade from full-time employment. The transition took years—reducing hours, delegating responsibilities, discovering that the organization continued functioning without my daily presence. My ego took some bruising in this discovery. I had imagined myself essential. Indispensable. The reality was more modest.
  2127|
  2128|What filled the space that work had occupied? At first, nothing. I wandered the house, restless, searching for purpose. Cindy—patient Cindy—let me wander. She knew, better than I did, that this transition required time. That identity built over forty years could not be dismantled in a month.
  2129|
  2130|Slowly, new structures emerged. I took up photography seriously, not as a hobby but as a practice. Hours in the darkroom—yes, I still use film, still enjoy the alchemy of chemicals and light—producing images that no one needed but me. This was the point: to create without utility, without market, without external validation.
  2131|
  2132|I joined a makerspace. Learned 3D printing. Found myself fascinated by the technology—the precision of it, the democratization of manufacturing, the way complex forms could emerge from simple digital instructions. I printed toys for the grandchildren, replacement parts for household items, increasingly ambitious sculptures that accumulated on shelves and in corners.
  2133|
  2134|"You're like a kid with a new toy," Cindy observed, watching me calibrate a print that had failed three times already.
  2135|
  2136|"I am a kid with a new toy," I said. "That's precisely the point."
  2137|
  2138|And there was the AI, of course. The technology that had seemed science fiction when I was young—talking computers, machines that could write and reason and create—now commonplace. I experimented with the systems, not to replace my own thinking but to extend it. To see what these tools could do, where they failed, what they revealed about human cognition by their limitations.
  2139|
  2140|Cindy worried, sometimes, that I was retreating into technology. That the screens and printers and code were replacing human connection. But she misunderstood. The technology was a bridge, not a wall. A way of staying engaged with a world that was changing faster than my aging brain could naturally adapt.
  2141|
  2142|## Two Homes, One Life
  2143|
  2144|We split our time now. Michigan in the summers, when the lakes are swimmable and the gardens are lush. Florida in the winters, when the cold becomes an assault and the bones ache for warmth.
  2145|
  2146|The arrangement suits us both. I need the change of seasons, the reminder that time is passing, that nothing remains static. Cindy needs the warmth, the ease of winter days without the struggle of ice and snow. We have learned—finally, in our seventies—to accommodate each other's needs without resentment.
  2147|
  2148|The Michigan house is the one we bought together, early in our marriage. It carries no ghosts. No memories of Nancy in the kitchen or the bedroom. This was intentional. We wanted a space that belonged entirely to us, to the partnership we were building.
  2149|
  2150|The Florida condo came later, purchased when the winters grew too hard and the grandchildren too distant. It is smaller, easier to maintain, close to friends who have made similar migrations. We have built a community there—other couples who have reached this stage, who understand the particular challenges and pleasures of lives in their final chapters.
  2151|
  2152|I travel between these homes with the ease of long practice. Each contains what I need: space to work, space to think, space to be with Cindy in the comfortable silence of established partnership. We have been married more than twenty years now. Long enough that the marriage feels inevitable, permanent, as much a fact of existence as gravity or breathing.
  2153|
  2154|## The Partnership Mature
  2155|
  2156|Cindy has changed me. I want to be clear about this, because it matters. Not in the ways Nancy changed me—those changes were formative, foundational, the construction of the person I became during adulthood. Cindy's changes are different. Refinements. Adjustments. The sanding of rough edges I did not know I possessed.
  2157|
  2158|She has taught me patience. I was always eager to solve problems, to move forward, to progress. Cindy moves more slowly, considers more carefully, resists the impulse toward immediate action. I have learned—am still learning—to match her pace. To discover that not every problem requires a solution. That some problems simply need to be sat with, acknowledged, allowed to resolve themselves in their own time.
  2159|
  2160|She has taught me the value of maintenance. I was always focused on the new project, the next challenge, the achievement waiting to be unlocked. Cindy tends to what already exists. The friendships that need nurturing. The home that needs care. The body that needs attention. I have become, through her example, more attentive to the ongoing work of sustaining what is already good.
  2161|
  2162|And she has taught me about second chances. Not in the abstract—everyone speaks of second chances—but in the concrete daily reality of them. The decision, made anew each morning, to choose this life. To choose each other. To believe that love remains possible even after failure, even after loss, even after the hopes of youth have been modified by the experience of age.
  2163|
  2164|We do not talk about these things. Not directly. But I know them. I feel them in the way she brings me tea without asking, in the way she listens to my rambles about 3D printing tolerances or AI capabilities, in the way she reaches for my hand during movies or drives or ordinary evenings at home.
  2165|
  2166|This is what partnership looks like in its mature form. Not the drama of new love, the intensity of early connection. Something quieter. More durable. The accumulated weight of shared experience, shared memory, shared intention.
  2167|
  2168|## The Machines and Me
  2169|
  2170|I spend more time with machines than I once did. The 3D printer humming in the basement. The computer screen displaying code I am learning to write—slowly, badly, but with genuine engagement. The AI systems I query and test and occasionally argue with.
  2171|
  2172|Some of my contemporaries find this sad. They see technology as a retreat from human connection, a substitution of artificial interaction for the real thing. I understand this concern. I have felt the seduction of screens, the way they can replace presence with performance, depth with breadth.
  2173|
  2174|But I do not believe this is inevitable. Technology is a tool. Like any tool, it can be used well or poorly. The question is not whether to engage with these systems, but how. Whether we maintain sovereignty over our attention and intention, or surrender them to the design of systems that profit from our distraction.
  2175|
  2176|I use the AI to extend my thinking. To access information that would have required hours of research in my youth. To test ideas, to explore possibilities, to learn new skills at an age when conventional wisdom says learning stops. The AI does not replace my judgment. It augments it.
  2177|
  2178|The 3D printing connects me to making, to the physical world, to the satisfaction of creating tangible objects from digital designs. It reminds me of my father's garage, of the boat we built together, of the pleasure that comes from seeing form emerge from raw material through the application of skill and attention.
  2179|
  2180|And the photography—film photography, with its demands for patience and precision—grounds me in the analog world even as I explore the digital one. The darkroom requires presence. You cannot rush development. You must pay attention to temperature, to timing, to the subtle changes in the chemistry. It is a meditation, this work. A practice of attention in an age of distraction.
  2181|
  2182|## The Fallibility of Memory
  2183|
  2184|I have been writing this memoir for some time now. Recording the stories, the events, the people who have shaped my life. And I have discovered something unsettling: I am not certain of my memories.
  2185|
  2186|Not that they are false, exactly. But that they are constructed. Reconstructed. Each time I recall an event, I alter it slightly—emphasizing certain details, minimizing others, shaping the narrative to fit my current understanding of who I am and what my life means.
  2187|
  2188|The conversation with Nancy on the night she died. I have told this story many times. Written it in these pages. And yet, when I focus intently on the memory, I find gaps. Was it evening or afternoon? Did we speak in the bedroom or the living room? Did she say "you were the best part of my life" or "you were the best thing in my life"? The difference matters, somehow. The exact words matter.
  2189|
  2190|But I cannot retrieve them with certainty. What I have is an impression. A feeling. The sense of that moment, if not its precise coordinates in space and time.
  2191|
  2192|This is the nature of memory. Not a recording, but a reenactment. Not a file to be accessed, but a performance to be staged anew each time it is recalled. The self that remembers is different from the self that experienced. The context of remembering—my current situation, my current concerns—shapes what is recalled and how it is understood.
  2193|
  2194|I have tried to be honest in these pages. To tell the truth as I remember it, while acknowledging that memory is not the same as truth. That the stories we tell about our lives become, in some sense, the lives themselves. We are not merely the sum of our experiences, but the sum of our interpretations of those experiences. The narrative we construct shapes the person we become.
  2195|
  2196|This memoir, then, is not only a record. It is an act of becoming. By writing these stories, I am making myself. Defining who I have been so that who I am might be clearer. Leaving a trace for those who come after, so they might understand—if understanding is possible—the path that led to their existence.
  2197|
  2198|## What Remains Unwritten
  2199|
  2200|I am in my late seventies now. The actuarial tables give me another decade, perhaps two if I am lucky and my genes cooperate. Enough time, potentially, to see Emma graduate from high school. To meet great-grandchildren, if my grandchildren choose to have children and choose to have them while I am still here to meet them.
  2201|
  2202|But not enough time to see the future that is coming. The world in 2050, 2060, 2070. The technologies that will transform daily life. The challenges—climate, political instability, the ongoing project of human cooperation across difference—that will shape the decades ahead.
  2203|
  2204|I find I do not mind this limitation. The future was never mine to experience. It belongs to the young, to those who will build it, suffer it, transform it. My role is to bear witness to what has been, to offer what wisdom I have accumulated, to step aside when the time comes and let the next generation take the lead.
  2205|
  2206|There is freedom in this acceptance. I no longer need to plan for a future I will not see. I can focus on the present—the actual present, the only time any of us ever truly inhabit. The morning coffee with Cindy. The afternoon with Emma, building Lego structures that she designs and I help execute. The evening walk, watching the sun set over water, feeling the air cool as day transitions to night.
  2207|
  2208|These moments are enough. More than enough. They are everything.
  2209|
  2210|## What I Would Tell Them
  2211|
  2212|If I could gather my grandchildren—Emma, and Robbie's children, and any who may come after—and tell them what I have learned, it would be this:
  2213|
  2214|First, that life is harder than you expect and more beautiful than you imagine. The difficulties will test you. The beauty will sustain you. Do not let either surprise you into despair or complacency.
  2215|
  2216|Second, that love is not a feeling but a practice. It requires attention, maintenance, the daily choice to show up for the people you have committed to. The feeling comes and goes. The practice remains.
  2217|
  2218|Third, that failure is not the opposite of success but its prerequisite. You will fail. Repeatedly. The question is not whether you fail but what you learn, how you adapt, whether you have the resilience to try again.
  2219|
  2220|Fourth, that technology is a tool, not a solution. It can amplify human capability for good or ill. The direction depends on human choices, human values, human wisdom. Do not surrender your agency to the machines. Maintain your judgment. Use the tools; do not let them use you.
  2221|
  2222|Fifth, that memory is fallible and stories are powerful. Pay attention to the narratives you construct about your life. They will shape who you become. Choose interpretations that serve your growth, that honor your struggles, that leave room for redemption and change.
  2223|
  2224|Sixth, that time is the only genuine currency. How you spend your hours is how you spend your life. Guard them jealously. Give them generously to what matters. Do not let them be stolen by distraction or obligation or the expectations of others.
  2225|
  2226|And finally, that you are part of something larger than yourself. A family, a community, a species, a planet. Your actions ripple outward in ways you cannot foresee. Act with this knowledge. Leave the world better than you found it, if you can. At minimum, do not make it worse.
  2227|
  2228|## The Unwritten Future
  2229|
  2230|I do not know how this story ends. None of us do. I could die tomorrow, or I could live another twenty years. The future is unwritten, as it has always been, as it will always be.
  2231|
  2232|What I know is this: I have lived fully. I have loved deeply. I have built things—physical and relational—that will outlast me. I have survived losses that seemed unsurvivable and discovered, each time, that survival was possible. That growth was possible. That joy could return even after profound grief.
  2233|
  2234|I have been lucky. Luck matters more than we like to admit. I was born in a time and place of relative peace and prosperity. I had parents who cared, teachers who challenged, partners who loved. I had work that mattered and children who became adults I am proud to know.
  2235|
  2236|But I have also worked. Have also chosen, again and again, to engage rather than withdraw, to build rather than destroy, to hope rather than despair. These choices were mine. The effort was mine. Whatever success I have achieved contains both the gift of fortune and the fruits of labor.
  2237|
  2238|Cindy is calling me now. Dinner is ready. The evening stretches ahead—ordinary, precious, irreplaceable. I will close this document, go downstairs, join my wife at the table. We will eat, talk, perhaps watch something on the screen or read in companionable silence. Tomorrow will bring its own challenges and pleasures.
  2239|
  2240|The memoir will remain incomplete, as all memoirs must. The story continues as long as life continues. New chapters are being written even now, in the choices I make, the relationships I tend, the small daily acts that constitute a life.
  2241|
  2242|But I have said what I needed to say. Recorded what I wanted remembered. Offered what I hoped might be useful to those who come after.
  2243|
  2244|The rest is unwritten. The rest is mystery. The rest belongs to time, which continues its indifferent march regardless of our wishes, our fears, our hopes.
  2245|
  2246|I am ready. Whatever comes, I am ready.
  2247|
  2248|And if you are reading this—if you have made it this far through my ramblings and reflections—thank you. For your attention. For your time. For the connection that exists between us, writer and reader, past and future, the living and the yet-to-be-born.
  2249|
  2250|The future is unwritten. But we have the power, each of us, to try and make it a good one.
  2251|
  2252|That is enough. That must be enough.
  2253|
  2254|---
  2255|
  2256|*Physiological Context:* At seventy-three, Bob's brain had undergone significant structural changes—cortical thinning, reduced white matter integrity, a slowing of neural signal transmission that manifested as slightly longer reaction times and a reduced ability to process multiple streams of information simultaneously. Working memory capacity had diminished, making it harder to hold many items in mind at once. Crystallized intelligence, however—the accumulated knowledge and wisdom built over decades—remained robust or even continued to grow. The hippocampus, where episodic memories are formed and retrieved, was showing the wear of seven decades of heavy use, making recall of specific details less reliable even as the meaning and emotional resonance of experiences remained vivid. Bob's sleep architecture had shifted, with less deep sleep and more fragmented nights, affecting memory consolidation. His brain was old, but it was still his brain—still capable of insight, still shaped by the extraordinary life it had lived.
  2257|
  2258|*Historical Context:* Bob was seventy-three in 2006, writing this memoir in the quiet of his later years. His second marriage to Cindy was well-established, the grandchildren were a daily source of wonder, and the urgency that had driven him through his career and his first marriage had given way to a different kind of engagement—one rooted in presence rather than ambition. He had outlived many of his contemporaries and had learned to carry that weight, as everyone does eventually. His children were adults with their own children. His parents were long gone. The country had changed in ways he sometimes struggled to understand. And yet he was still here, still writing, still reaching toward whatever came next.
  2259|
  2260|---
  2261|
  2262|# Chapter 11: The Derby
  2263|
  2264|*What We Learned at the Track*
  2265|
  2266|The county fair stretched out before us like a carnival of dreams, the smell of popcorn and cotton candy mixing with the crisp autumn air in a way that made every childlike anticipation bubble up inside me. I was twelve years old, and my father had brought me to the Derby that year—the first time he'd taken me to the horse races, treating me like I was old enough to understand what we were about to witness.
  2267|
  2268|"Stay close, Bobby," my father said, his large hand resting on my shoulder. "It's easy to get lost in a crowd this size."
  2269|
  2270|The fairgrounds were overwhelming in the best possible way. Vendors shouted their wares. Children shrieked with joy on carnival rides. The smell of fried dough and roasted peanuts hung in the air like a delicious cloud. But what drew my attention most was the race track itself—a oval of dirt and grass that seemed enormous to my twelve-year-old eyes, surrounded by wooden fences and filled with an energy that hummed through the ground and up into my bones.
  2271|
  2272|My father had been coming to the Derby for years. He knew the routines, the rhythms, the people. He exchanged nods with other regulars, placed his bets with the confidence of a man who had done this dozens of times, and led me to a spot near the railing where we could see the horses as they rounded the track.
  2273|
  2274|"See that one?" he said, pointing to a dark brown horse being led to the starting gate. "Number seven. That's our horse."
  2275|
  2276|I studied the horse with the intense focus only a child can muster. The animal's coat gleamed in the afternoon sun, muscles rippling beneath the surface as a groom adjusted its bridle. The horse tossed its head impatiently, nostrils flaring, as if it knew what was about to happen and couldn't wait to get started.
  2277|
  2278|"Why that one?" I asked.
  2279|
  2280|"Because he's been behind all race, Bobby. Every time. But he keeps running. Every single time, he finds something extra at the end." My father's eyes never left the horse. "That's the kind of horse you bet on. Not the favorite. The one who never gives up."
  2281|
  2282|The starting gate opened with a metallic clatter, and suddenly the air was filled with the thunder of hooves. Six horses exploded out of the gates, their powerful legs churning up dirt and dust that drifted across the track like brown smoke. The crowd erupted in cheers and shouts, each spectator pulling for their chosen horse, the noise drowning out everything else except the pounding of my own heart.
  2283|
  2284|Number seven was behind. I could see it clearly—the dark brown horse was running hard, but three other horses had pulled ahead, their jockeys urging them forward with whips and voices. My father didn't react. He just watched, his face calm, as if he already knew how this story would end.
  2285|
  2286|"Come on, boy," he muttered, barely audible above the crowd. "You've got it in you. Show them what you've got."
  2287|
  2288|The horses rounded the far turn, and I watched number seven's head bob up and down as the animal gave everything it had. The lead horses were tiring—I could see it in the way their legs were starting to shorten, their powerful strides becoming more labored. But number seven was still running, still pushing, still refusing to accept that today wasn't his day.
  2289|
  2290|And then, something incredible happened.
  2291|
  2292|Number seven began to gain. Slowly at first, then faster, as if the horse had found some hidden reserve of energy. The crowd noticed too—the noise shifted, became something more like astonishment, and I heard people around us start to cheer for the dark brown horse that was now charging up on the outside.
  2293|
  2294|"He's doing it!" I screamed, grabbing my father's arm. "He's doing it!"
  2295|
  2296|My father didn't say anything. He just smiled—that quiet, knowing smile I would remember for the rest of my life—as number seven surged forward and crossed the finish line first, a full length ahead of the second-place horse.
  2297|
  2298|"That's how you win, son," my father said, slapping me on the back. "You never give up, no matter how far behind you are. The race isn't over until it's over. Remember that."
  2299|
  2300|I remember that day for the rest of my life. Not because we won money—we didn't, as it turned out my father had bet on the wrong horse in the end, having changed his mind at the last moment out of some superstitious habit—but because of the lesson I learned sitting on that wooden railing, watching that dark brown horse refuse to accept defeat.
  2301|
  2302|In life, like in horse racing, it's not about the start. It's about the finish.
  2303|
  2304|---
  2305|
  2306|## The Weight of Expectations
  2307|
  2308|Being at the Derby taught me something else too—the weight of expectations. My father had pointed at that horse with such certainty, such belief that it would win. When it didn't, there was a brief flicker of disappointment in his eyes before he smiled and shrugged.
  2309|
  2310|"Win some, lose some," he said. "That's how it goes. Doesn't change anything. We'll be back next year."
  2311|
  2312|But I saw that flicker. I understood, even then, that my father carried expectations like everyone else. He wanted to be right. He wanted to win. And when he didn't, it mattered to him—even if he would never admit it aloud.
  2313|
  2314|Life is like that, I learned. You can point at your future with all the certainty in the world, but sometimes the horse you bet on doesn't come in. The job you expected to get goes to someone else. The business you've built hits a wall you didn't see. The relationship you've invested in ends in ways you never imagined.
  2315|

{"success": true, "name": "openrouter-image-generation-workflow", "description": "Comprehensive workflow for generating images via OpenRouter API with Flux.2 model, including background processing, error handling, and HTML integration", "tags": ["image_gen", "openrouter", "workflow", "flux", "background-processing"], "related_skills": ["openrouter-image-generation"], "content": "--- name: openrouter-image-generation-workflow description: Comprehensive workflow for generating images via OpenRouter API with Flux.2 model, including background processing, error handling, and HTML integration version: 1.0.0 author: Hermes Agent license: MIT metadata: hermes: tags: [image_gen, openrouter, workflow, flux, background-processing] related_skills: [openrouter-image-generation] --- # OpenRouter Image Generation Workflow This skill documents the complete approach for generating images via OpenRouter API with Flux.2 model, including background processing, error handling, and HTML integration. ## When to Use This Workflow Use this workflow when you need to generate multiple images via OpenRouter API and integrate them into HTML documents. This approach is particularly valuable for: - Generating book covers and chapter headers - Batch image generation with progress tracking - Robust error handling and recovery - HTML document integration ## Key Components ### 1. Background Processing ```python # Run the script in the background to avoid blocking terminal(background=True, command="python /path/to/script.py > /tmp/log.txt 2>&1 &", notify_on_complete=True) ``` ### 2. API Request Function ```python def generate_image(prompt, output_path, api_key, model="black-forest-labs/flux.2-max"): """ Generate a single image and save to file. Handles API errors, timeouts, and file verification. """ url = "https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions" headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}'} payload = { "model": model, "messages": [ {"role": "system", "content": "You are an AI assistant that generates images."}, {"role": "user", "content": f"Generate an image:\\n\\n{prompt}\\n\\nReturn as base64 PNG."} ], "modalities": ["image"] } try: response = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=120) response.raise_for_status() result = response.json() # Extract image data choices = result.get('choices', []) if not choices or 'message' not in choices[0]: raise ValueError("Invalid response structure") images = choices[0]['message'].get('images', []) if not images: raise ValueError("No images in response") img_data = images[0] if not isinstance(img_data, dict) or 'image_url' not in img_data: raise ValueError("Invalid image data") img_url = img_data['image_url'] if not isinstance(img_url, dict) or 'url' not in img_url: raise ValueError("No image URL provided") img_url_str = img_url['url'] if not img_url_str.startswith('data:image/png;base64,'): raise ValueError("Unexpected image format") # Decode and save img_b64 = img_url_str.split(',')[1] img_bytes = base64.b64decode(img_b64) with open(output_path, 'wb') as f: f.write(img_bytes) # Verify file exists if not Path(output_path).exists(): raise FileNotFoundError("Failed to save image file") return output_path except Exception as e: # Log error and return None for retry print(f"Error generating image: {e}") return None ``` ### 3. Batch Processing with Progress Tracking ```python def generate_images_batch(prompts, output_dir, api_key, model="black-forest-labs/flux.2-max"): """ Generate multiple images with progress tracking and error recovery. Runs in background with notifications on completion. """ success_count = 0 fail_count = 0 failures = [] for name, prompt in prompts.items(): output_path = Path(output_dir) / f"{name}.png" # Generate image result = generate_image(prompt, str(output_path), api_key, model) if result: print(f"✅ Generated {name}") success_count += 1 else: print(f"❌ Failed to generate {name}") fail_count += 1 failures.append(name) # Delay to avoid rate limiting time.sleep(3) print(f"\nSummary: {success_count} succeeded, {fail_count} failed") if failures: print(f"Failed: {', '.join(failures)}") return success_count, fail_count, failures ``` ### 4. HTML Integration ```python def insert_images_into_html(html_path, image_dir, mapping): """ Insert generated images into HTML document. mapping: {placeholder_name: image_filename} """ with open(html_path, 'r') as f: html_content = f.read() for placeholder, image_file in mapping.items(): img_path = Path(image_dir) / image_file if not img_path.exists(): print(f"Warning: {image_file} not found") continue # Create img tag img_tag = f'' # Find insertion point using regex patterns if placeholder == 'cover': # Insert after cover-author div in cover section pattern = r'(
.*?)(
.*?
)' match = re.search(pattern, html_content, re.DOTALL) if match: new_content = match.group(1) + match.group(2) + '\n ' + img_tag + '\n
' html_content = html_content.replace(match.group(0), new_content) print(f"Inserted cover image") elif placeholder.startswith('chapter'): # Insert after chapter heading h3 tag chapter_num = placeholder.replace('chapter', '') heading = None if chapter_num == '1': heading = "The Builder's Blood" elif chapter_num == '2': heading = "The Navy Way" elif chapter_num == '4': heading = "The Garage Stays Open" elif chapter_num == '5': heading = "The TV Repair Shop" elif chapter_num == '6': heading = "The Engineering of Everything" elif chapter_num == '7': heading = "Chapter xx: Engineer vs. Executive" # Fallback else: heading = f"Chapter {chapter_num}" pattern = rf']*>{heading}' match = re.search(pattern, html_content) if match: new_content = html_content.replace( match.group(0), match.group(0) + '\n' + img_tag + '\n' ) html_content = new_content print(f"Inserted chapter {chapter_num} image") # Write modified HTML with open(html_path, 'w') as f: f.write(html_content) # Remove duplicate images if any cleanup_duplicate_images(html_path) ``` ### 5. Duplicate Cleanup ```python def cleanup_duplicate_images(html_path): """ Remove duplicate image tags that may have been inserted multiple times. """ with open(html_path, 'r') as f: html_content = f.read() # Find all cover image tags cover_img_pattern = r'' matches = list(re.finditer(cover_img_pattern, html_content)) if len(matches) > 1: # Keep only the first one after cover div cover_div_end = html_content.find('', html_content.find('
')) if cover_div_end != -1: # Find first cover img after cover div first_valid_img = None for match in matches: if match.start() > cover_div_end: first_valid_img = match break if first_valid_img: # Remove all others for match in matches: if match != first_valid_img: html_content = html_content.replace(match.group(0), '') print(f"Removed {len(matches)-1} duplicate cover images") # Write back with open(html_path, 'w') as f: f.write(html_content) ``` ## Lessons Learned from Trial and Error ### 1. API Response Structure - The image URL is deeply nested in the JSON response - Need to handle cases where fields might be missing - Base64 data URL requires stripping the prefix before decoding ### 2. Error Handling - API calls can fail for many reasons (network, rate limiting, model issues) - Always verify files are created successfully - Implement retry logic for transient failures - Log errors with context for debugging ### 3. HTML Integration - Understanding the HTML structure is crucial for correct image placement - Use regex patterns that are specific enough but flexible - Handle cases where insertion points might not exist - Clean up duplicates from multiple insertion attempts ### 4. Performance Considerations - Running in background prevents timeouts from blocking - Include delays between requests to avoid rate limiting - Verify file existence before proceeding - Use efficient string operations for HTML manipulation ### 5. Robustness - Always check if files exist before trying to read them - Handle different image formats gracefully - Provide meaningful error messages - Clean up temporary files if needed ## When This Approach Works Well - **Batch image generation**: Perfect for generating multiple images with different prompts - **HTML integration**: Seamlessly integrates generated images into existing HTML documents - **Error recovery**: Handles failures gracefully and continues processing - **Progress tracking**: Provides clear feedback on success/failure rates ## Limitations - **API dependent**: Requires OpenRouter API access and a valid API key - **Model specific**: Uses Flux.2 model; may need adjustments for other models - **HTML structure dependent**: Requires understanding of target HTML structure - **Rate limits**: Subject to OpenRouter's rate limits ## Best Practices 1. **Test with a single image first** before batch processing 2. **Include proper error handling** for all API interactions 3. **Verify file creation** after each generation 4. **Use appropriate delays** between requests to avoid rate limiting 5. **Clean up duplicates** if running multiple times 6. **Monitor progress** and log errors for debugging ## Related Skills - `openrouter-image-generation` (basic skill) - `html-integration` (for HTML manipulation) - `background-processing` (for running tasks asynchronously)", "path": "openrouter-image-generation-workflow/SKILL.md", "skill_dir": "/home/bob/.hermes/skills/openrouter-image-generation-workflow", "linked_files": null, "usage_hint": null, "required_environment_variables": [], "required_commands": [], "missing_required_environment_variables": [], "missing_credential_files": [], "missing_required_commands": [], "setup_needed": false, "setup_skipped": false, "readiness_status": "available", "metadata": {"hermes": {"tags": ["image_gen", "openrouter", "workflow", "flux", "background-processing"], "related_skills": ["openrouter-image-generation"]}}}

{"success": true, "name": "memoir-publishing-workflow", "description": "Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration.", "tags": ["memoir", "publishing", "formatting", "transitions", "PDF", "HTML", "WeasyPrint", "OpenRouter", "AI-generation", "image-creation"], "related_skills": [], "content": "--- name: memoir-publishing-workflow version: 2.0.0 description: Comprehensive approach for transforming raw memoirs into professionally formatted books with enhanced transitions, proper publishing details, and AI integration. tags: [memoir, publishing, formatting, transitions, PDF, HTML, WeasyPrint, OpenRouter, AI-generation, image-creation] depends: [add_transitions_to_unwritten_future, manuscript-conversion-pipeline, manuscript-restructuring] --- # Memoir Publishing Workflow **Skill for:** Systematically transforming a raw memoir manuscript into a professionally formatted, published-quality book (HTML/PDF) with enhanced transitions, proper front/back matter, AI-generated images, and print-ready output. ## Overview This skill provides a comprehensive approach for converting raw memoir content into a print-ready format, including: - **Manuscript preparation** - Content review, editing, and structural organization - **Formatting & layout** - HTML/CSS styling for professional appearance - **Image generation** - AI-created chapter illustrations and cover art - **PDF conversion** - Multiple methods for print-ready output - **Quality assurance** - Verification and testing procedures - **Delivery** - File preparation and distribution The workflow combines traditional publishing techniques with modern AI tools to create high-quality books efficiently. ## When to Use - When preparing a memoir for publication - When enhancing narrative flow with historical context - When formatting books for print or digital distribution - When working with limited formatting tools - When creating professional-quality books without expensive software ## Prerequisites - Raw manuscript content (Markdown or text format) - Basic understanding of book structure (front matter, chapters, back matter) - Access to image generation tools (OpenRouter recommended) - PDF conversion capability (WeasyPrint preferred, alternatives available) - Python environment for automation (optional but helpful) ## Phase 1: Manuscript Preparation ### Content Review Process 1. **Read through complete manuscript** to understand narrative flow and identify gaps 2. **Check for consistency** in voice, tense, and perspective throughout 3. **Verify historical facts** and timeline accuracy 4. **Evaluate transition quality** between chapters and parts 5. **Assess emotional impact** and reader engagement ### Editing Approach - **Structural editing**: Ensure logical chapter progression and proper sequencing - **Line editing**: Improve sentence flow, readability, and style - **Transition enhancement**: Replace placeholders with rich, personal reflections - **Fact-checking**: Verify historical events and personal details - **Sensitivity review**: Ensure respectful representation of all people and events ### Key Deliverables - Clean, edited manuscript file (Markdown format) - Chapter-by-chapter analysis report - Transition quality assessment - Historical context verification - Sensitivity review notes ## Phase 2: Formatting & Layout ### HTML Structure ```html Memoir Title
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
...
``` ### CSS Styling Specifications ```css /* Base styles */ body { font-family: 'Times New Roman', serif; margin: 2.5cm; /* Standard print margins */ line-height: 1.5; color: #333; max-width: 100%; hyphens: auto; } /* Page setup for A4 */ @page { size: A4; margin: 2.5cm; } /* Chapter headings */ .chapter { page-break-before: always; margin-top: 3cm; } .chapter-number { font-size: 2em; font-weight: bold; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.1em; margin-bottom: 0.5em; } .chapter-title { font-size: 1.5em; font-weight: normal; margin-bottom: 1em; } /* Transitions */ .transition { font-style: italic; margin: 2em 0; padding: 1em 2em; border-left: 3px solid #ccc; background: #f9f9f9; } /* Page numbers */ @bottom-center { content: counter(page); font-size: 0.9em; color: #666; } /* Headers */ @top-left { content: "The Future is Unwritten"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } @top-right { content: "Robert Mills"; font-size: 0.8em; color: #999; } ``` ### Special Elements - **Transitions**: 10-20 sentence passages between chapters - **Historical context**: Integrated seamlessly into narrative - **Physiological effects**: Described in accessible, engaging language - **Images**: Placeholder positions with captions - **Drop caps**: First letter of each chapter enlarged and styled - **Part openings**: Special formatting for major section divisions ## Phase 3: Image Generation ### Image Types Required 1. **Cover Image** - Professional, eye-catching design 2. **Chapter Illustrations** - One per chapter (black and white sketches) 3. **Epilogue Image** - Reflective closing image ### Prompt Engineering Approach For each image, create specific prompts based on chapter content: **Cover Prompt Structure:** ``` Create a professional book cover for the memoir "[TITLE]" by [AUTHOR]. The cover should feature: - [Key visual elements representing main themes] - [Color scheme and mood description] - [Typography requirements] - [Style guidelines: modern/classic, minimal/detailed] - Aspect ratio: 2:3 (standard book cover) ``` **Chapter Sketch Prompt Structure:** ``` [Description of scene or symbol from chapter]. Style: Black and white pencil sketch, hand-drawn, with shading and texture, suitable for a memoir chapter header. ``` ### Image Integration - Save generated images as PNG files (300 DPI for print) - Place images at chapter beginnings (approx. 3-4 inches wide) - Add descriptive captions when appropriate - Ensure consistent style across all illustrations - Optimize file sizes for web and print versions ## Phase 4: PDF Conversion ### WeasyPrint Conversion ```python from weasyprint import HTML # Basic conversion HTML('manuscript.html').write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With custom CSS for print-specific styling HTML('manuscript.html', stylesheets=['print.css']).write_pdf('memoir.pdf') # With additional options HTML( 'manuscript.html', stylesheets=['style.css', 'print.css'], url_fetcher=my_url_fetcher # For handling local image paths ).write_pdf( 'memoir.pdf', zoom=1.0, # Adjust as needed image_resolution=300 # DPI for images ) ``` ### Alternative Methods 1. **Browser Print**: Open HTML in browser and use "Print to PDF" 2. **wkhtmltopdf**: Command-line tool for batch processing ```bash wkhtmltopdf book.html book.pdf ``` 3. **Pandoc**: Universal document converter ```bash pandoc book.html -o book.pdf ``` 4. **PrinceXML**: Commercial alternative with excellent CSS support ```bash prince book.html -o book.pdf ``` ### Print-Ready Settings - **Bleeds**: 0.125 inches (if required by printer) - **Resolution**: 300 DPI for images - **Color Profile**: CMYK for professional printing - **Fonts**: Embed all fonts or use web-safe alternatives - **Accessibility**: Add semantic HTML structure for screen readers ## Phase 5: Quality Assurance ### Content Verification Checklist - [ ] All chapters present and in correct order - [ ] Transitions are meaningful and well-placed - [ ] Images match chapter content and are properly positioned - [ ] Page numbers correct and consistent throughout - [ ] Table of contents matches chapter pages - [ ] Front matter properly formatted and in correct order - [ ] Copyright and ISBN information included - [ ] Back matter complete (epilogue, author bio, etc.) ### Technical Checks - [ ] PDF renders correctly on multiple devices and PDF readers - [ ] Fonts display properly (embedded/embeddable) - [ ] Images are high resolution (300 DPI) and clear - [ ] Margins are correct for chosen printer specifications - [ ] No text is cut off or obscured by images - [ ] Hyperlinks work correctly (if digital version) - [ ] File size appropriate for distribution method ### Proofreading - [ ] Spelling and grammar checked using multiple tools - [ ] Punctuation consistent throughout document - [ ] Capitalization follows style guide - [ ] Chapter titles match across all instances - [ ] Page breaks occur at appropriate locations - [ ] No widows/orphans in text blocks - [ ] Consistent use of italics/bold for emphasis ## Phase 6: Delivery ### File Preparation - **Print PDF**: High-resolution, CMYK color profile, proper bleeds - **Ebook PDF**: Optimized for screen reading, smaller file size - **Source Files**: HTML, CSS, and Markdown originals - **Image Files**: Original AI-generated images and optimized versions - **Cover Files**: Print-ready cover with spine and back cover ### Distribution Methods 1. **Direct Download**: Provide zip file with all assets 2. **Cloud Storage**: Upload to Google Drive, Dropbox, etc. 3. **Print Service**: Upload directly to print-on-demand service 4. **Email**: Send files to publisher or printer 5. **Website**: Host on author website for download ### Platform-Specific Requirements - **Amazon KDP**: Specific file formats and bleed settings - **IngramSpark**: PDF/X-1a compliance for professional printing - **Local Printer**: Custom specifications as needed - **Ebook Platforms**: EPUB/MOBI formats if needed ## Tools & Technologies ### Required Tools - **Text Editor**: VS Code, Sublime Text, or similar - **HTML/CSS**: Basic knowledge for formatting - **Python**: For automation scripts (optional but helpful) - **WeasyPrint**: PDF conversion library (preferred) - **Image Generation API**: OpenRouter or similar - **Web Browser**: For testing and PDF printing ### Optional Tools - **Git**: Version control for manuscript iterations - **Pandoc**: Format conversion between document types - **Calibre**: Ebook management and conversion - **Adobe Acrobat**: Advanced PDF editing and checking - **Photoshop/GIMP**: Image editing if needed ## Best Practices ### Content Creation - Write transitions that connect emotionally with readers - Use historical events to provide context, not overwhelm - Balance personal stories with broader themes - Show, don't tell - use sensory details and specific examples - Maintain consistent voice throughout the memoir ### Technical Implementation - Test PDF conversion early and often with sample chapters - Keep original AI prompts for future image regeneration - Maintain version control for all manuscript iterations - Create backup copies of all generated files - Document any custom formatting requirements ### Quality Control - Get feedback from beta readers before finalizing - Print a proof copy before mass production - Check color accuracy if using color images - Verify all legal requirements (copyright, ISBN, etc.) - Test accessibility features for digital versions ## Troubleshooting ### Common Issues & Solutions **Issue**: Images not generating properly **Solution**: Refine prompts with more specific details, try different AI models, adjust parameters **Issue**: PDF formatting breaks or looks wrong **Solution**: Check CSS for print-specific rules, ensure proper page breaks, validate HTML structure **Issue**: Transitions feel forced or unnatural **Solution**: Read aloud to test flow, get feedback from others, revise for natural language **Issue**: Historical details inaccurate **Solution**: Cross-reference multiple sources, consult experts if possible, add disclaimers if uncertain **Issue**: File sizes too large for distribution **Solution**: Optimize images (compress without losing quality), minimize CSS, remove unnecessary assets **Issue**: WeasyPrint not available or not working **Solution**: Use browser print method or install wkhtmltopdf as alternative **Issue**: Images not displaying in PDF **Solution**: Check file paths, ensure images are accessible, use absolute paths if needed ## Success Metrics - **Content Quality**: Positive feedback from beta readers and reviewers - **Technical Quality**: Professional appearance, no formatting errors - **Production Readiness**: Files accepted by print-on-demand services - **Reader Engagement**: Strong reviews, good sales performance - **Personal Satisfaction**: Author feels accurately represented ## Example Project Structure ``` memoir-project/ ├── manuscript/ │ ├── raw/ # Original content │ ├── edited/ # Edited manuscript │ └── final.md # Final Markdown ├── formatting/ │ ├── html/ # HTML files │ ├── css/ # CSS stylesheets │ └── templates/ # Layout templates ├── images/ │ ├── generated/ # AI-generated images │ ├── placeholders/ # Temporary placeholders │ └── final/ # Optimized images ├── pdf/ │ ├── drafts/ # Test PDFs │ ├── proofs/ # Proof copies │ └── final/ # Production PDFs ├── scripts/ # Automation scripts ├── docs/ # Documentation └── README.md # Project overview ``` ## Notes This workflow combines traditional publishing approaches with modern AI tools. The key is maintaining the author's voice while leveraging technology to enhance quality and efficiency. {"code":"import os, time, json, base64, requests, yaml
from pathlib import Path

base = Path('/home/bob/books/The_Unwritten_Future')
out_path = base / 'generated_images' / 'cover_moon_base_hitech.png'
config_path = Path.home() / '.hermes' / 'config.yaml'

cfg = yaml.safe_load(config_path.read_text())
api_key = cfg['model']['api_key']

prompt = '''Create a high-tech full-color book cover illustration for the memoir "The Future is Unwritten" by Robert Mills.

Scene:
A sophisticated human moon base at the lunar south pole under a star-filled black sky. Sleek domes, illuminated glass corridors, landing pads, communication towers, autonomous rovers, and subtle Earthrise in the background. The base should feel visionary, intelligent, hopeful, and elegant — not dystopian. Blend aerospace engineering realism with premium near-future design.

Style:
Cinematic, high-detail, sharp focus, premium publishing quality, rich color, blue-white-silver lighting with subtle gold accents, advanced technology interfaces visible through glass, polished metallic surfaces, realistic lunar regolith, dramatic but clean composition.

Composition:
Vertical 2:3 book-cover composition with strong central visual hierarchy and open negative space in the upper and lower center for title/subtitle typography. No curved old-fashioned cover styling. No mockup. No visible printed book object. This must look like a modern high-tech cover artwork.

Avoid:
cartoon look, fantasy castles, clutter, heavy text baked into the image, low detail, retro pulp style, warped structures, blurry elements.
'''

payload = {
    'model': 'google/gemini-2.5-flash-image',
    'messages': [
        {'role': 'user', 'content': prompt}
    ],
    'modalities': ['image']
}

url = 'https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/chat/completions'
headers = {
    'Authorization': f'Bearer {api_key}',
    'Content-Type': 'application/json',
    'HTTP-Referer': 'https://hermes.local',
    'X-Title': 'Hermes Cover Generator'
}

last_err = None
for attempt in range(1, 6):
    try:
        r = requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload, timeout=240)
        if r.status_code >= 500 or r.status_code == 429:
            raise RuntimeError(f'status {r.status_code}: {r.text[:500]}')
        r.raise_for_status()
        data = r.json()
        msg = data['choices'][0]['message']
        images = msg.get('images') or []
        if not images:
            raise RuntimeError('No images returned. Response snippet: ' + json.dumps(data)[:1200])
        img_url = images[0].get('image_url', {}).get('url', '')
        if not img_url.startswith('data:image/'):
            raise RuntimeError('Unexpected image URL format: ' + img_url[:120])
        b64 = img_url.split(',', 1)[1]
        out_path.write_bytes(base64.b64decode(b64))
        print(json.dumps({'ok': True, 'path': str(out_path), 'size': out_path.stat().st_size, 'attempt': attempt}))
        break
    except Exception as e:
        last_err = str(e)
        if attempt == 5:
            print(json.dumps({'ok': False, 'error': last_err}))
            raise
        sleep_s = 2 ** (attempt - 1)
        time.sleep(sleep_s)
"}

  "analysis": "This image is a high-detail, AI-generated digital illustration of a futuristic lunar colony. Below is a comprehensive description and an assessment of its suitability for a premium memoir cover.

### Detailed Description
*   **Foreground:** The lunar surface is depicted with realistic gray regolith, scattered rocks, and craters. Several small, multi-wheeled robotic rovers are in motion, leaving visible tracks in the dust. To the right, a sleek, angular spacecraft sits on a circular landing pad marked with glowing yellow rings.
*   **Midground:** The centerpiece is a sprawling lunar base consisting of several large geodesic glass domes. These domes are interconnected by translucent, pressurized tunnels that glow with a soft blue internal light. Inside the domes, hints of high-tech infrastructure and multi-level floors are visible. To the right, a central hub features a tall communications spire and various antennae.
*   **Background:** The desolate, mountainous lunar horizon stretches across the frame. A distant sun or bright light source on the right creates long, dramatic shadows.
*   **Sky/Space:** Dominating the upper center is a massive, detailed Earth in a "gibbous" phase, showing swirling white clouds, blue oceans, and brown landmasses. The surrounding space is a deep black, densely populated with stars and nebulae.
*   **Color Palette & Lighting:** The image uses a "cool" palette of deep blues, grays, and blacks, contrasted by the warm yellow of the landing pad and the bright white/blue of the Earth. The lighting is cinematic, with high-contrast shadows that give the structures a sense of scale and three-dimensionality.

### Assessment for a Premium Memoir Cover

**Suitability:**
The image is visually striking and fits the "high-tech full-color moon base" theme perfectly. It conveys a sense of wonder, isolation, and human achievement, which are common themes in memoirs about space exploration or futuristic visionaries.

**Pros:**
*   **High Detail:** The resolution and complexity of the structures make it look professional at first glance.
*   **Atmosphere:** The lighting and composition create a "premium" feel that would stand out on a bookshelf.
*   **Thematic Clarity:** There is no ambiguity about the setting; it is clearly a lunar colony.

**Flaws and Issues:**
While impressive, the image has several "AI artifacts" and composition issues that might undermine a "premium" feel upon closer inspection:

1.  **Nonsensical Architecture:** Some of the glowing blue tunnels lead to nowhere or merge awkwardly into the ground without a clear structural purpose. The tunnel in the bottom left, for example, seems to just end abruptly.
2.  **Perspective Inconsistencies:** The tracks left by the rovers in the foreground don't always align with the direction the wheels are facing. Some rovers appear to be floating slightly above the surface.
3.  **Baked-in Text/Symbols:** There are no legible words, but there are "gibberish" markings on the side of the central hub and the spacecraft that look like distorted text or logos—a common trait of AI generation.
4.  **Compositional Crowding:** The image is very "busy." For a book cover, you need "negative space" (empty areas) to place the title and author's name. Currently, the Earth, the domes, and the rovers occupy almost every focal point, making it difficult to overlay text without obscuring the best parts of the art.
5.  **Scale Issues:** The Earth appears unnaturally large in the sky compared to the horizon, which is a common artistic choice but may bother readers looking for scientific realism in a memoir.

### Conclusion
This image is an excellent **concept piece**, but it is **not quite ready for a premium memoir cover.** To make it professional, a graphic designer would need to:
*   Clean up the "gibberish" markings on the ships.
*   Fix the "dead-end" tunnels.
*   Expand the sky or the ground to create a dedicated space for the book title and author name so the text doesn't have to fight with the complex background."
